messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-affinity rollout (runtimes v2.14) and the quantization profile bump we saw a ~22% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the 8k chat workload. RPS steady, latency slightly up. :frowning:
kevin: when did the rollout happen? any hosts still on old kernels?
infra-bot: rollout: v2.14 -> active on pool: inference-gpu-3 between 1728996000 and 1728999800. Canary passed.
sandeep: reprod locally with the same nightly model (redwood/gptx-8k-q4) — can reproduce the hit-rate drop in the perf harness. Dumping a couple quick stats:
```
before: prefix_hit_rate=0.83
after:  prefix_hit_rate=0.65
KV keys seen: 1.2M -> 1.9M unique
```
maria: that's a big unique-key inflation. implies key canonicalization/normalization change or hash salt variance. Any code paths touched in last compile?
sandeep: two suspects: (1) attention kernel refactor changed the order of some float->fp16 ops which altered intermediate rounding on cached keys for quantized runtimes, (2) we shipped a tiny change to the key hashing function to use xxh64 seed based on buildid. The latter was intentional but shouldn't affect canonical keys across a rolling cluster.
kevin: can you paste the hashing snippet you ran?
sandeep: sure — this is the canonicalization step we run before storing keys:
```
// pseudo
string canonical_prefix = normalize_whitespace(strip_metadata(prefix));
uint64_t h = xxh64(canonical_prefix.data(), canonical_prefix.size(), SEED);
cache_key = format("%s:%016x", model_id, h);
```
maria: SEED there was supposed to be constant across builds but buildid->seed mapping got wired to runtime.kernel_variant in the new compile path. That would mean different hosts generate different seeds — hence key fragmentation. :eyes:
elaine: so it's not just precision differences, it's literally different seeds? that explains the big jump in uniques. What triggered seed mapping change?
sandeep: the compile pass added "kernel_affinity" as part of the runtime metadata fingerprint to improve routing. the key-gen helper mistakenly used fingerprint_hash as the seed. previous behavior used a process-global fixed seed (0x9e3779b97f4a7c15).
kevin: ok that's a bug. we need to avoid baking per-host metadata into the key salt. mitigation paths: rollback the new fingerprint->seed mapping, or preserve old seed in a compatibility mode and add a migration that recomputes keys for active prefixes. both have tradeoffs.
maria: rollback is fastest for user impact. can infra roll back the rollout to v2.13 on the affected pools?
infra-bot: initiating rollback on pool inference-gpu-3 now. ETA ~6m.
oliver: we should also add a monitoring alert to detect sudden increases in unique key counts — low false positives. I can file a follow-up.
sandeep: quick patch ready: keep SEED static unless an operator opt-in flag is set. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8421 — tests included for key canonicalization.
kevin: also add an e2e warmup job to pre-populate common prompts after rolling forward a fix — that'll help latency while clients warm caches.
maria: agreed. plan: 1) rollback to v2.13 (done by infra) 2) merge sandeep's patch + add e2e canonicalization test 3) rollout v2.14+patch to canary for 12h, monitor prefix_hit_rate and unique-key delta 4) add alert on unique-key > +10%/5m and add automation to run prefix rehash migration if operator opts in.
elaine: for post-mortem add: kernel_affinity fingerprinting in runtime metadata should be audit-guarded before touching keygen.
kevin: noted. Also adding a small perf test that compares prefix hashing pre/post compile on nightly CI.
maria: thanks everyone — infra says rollback started and should finish in ~4m. I'll keep this thread as the source of truth for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
